Kate / Marissa / Procurement team —

Thanks for the questions. Below are the legal/technical responses keyed to the items in your template. I focused on the items we anticipate being most material to MedHealth's DPO. If you'd like, we can convert these into the exact cells in your attached DPF spreadsheet.

1) Data controller/processor roles
- Redwood Inference: acts as Data Processor on behalf of customers when providing Hosted API and Dedicated managed services. For Private/on-prem deployments where the customer hosts the runtime, Redwood acts as a vendor providing software and limited control-plane services — responsibilities are detailed in our Private Deployment Addendum.

2) Transfer mechanisms (EU/UK -> US)
- Hosted API (default): Redwood relies on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (module-based SCCs, 2021) plus our internal technical controls. For UK transfers we apply the UK Addendum to the SCCs.
- DPF: Redwood is DPF-certified for our hosted inference service (certificate current as of 2026-04). DPF applies to specified categories of personal data processed within the hosted boundary — this includes request payloads and associated logs for customers using the hosted API.
- Where customers require, we are prepared to apply SCCs in combination with the DPF or as an alternative; we include SCCs by default for EU-hosted contracts unless a customer explicitly requests DPF-only approach.

3) Subprocessors and notification
- Current subprocessors (representative): Amazon Web Services (us-east-1, eu-west-1), Google Cloud Platform (europe-west4), FastRoute Networks (CDN), SegmentOps (metrics/observability). Full list attached.
- Notification cadence: quarterly bulletin; critical changes notified 30 days prior to onboarding.

4) Data usage and training
- Redwood does NOT use customer data to improve model weights or training datasets. We may use aggregated telemetry for product ops with strict de-identification. This is contractually enforceable in our DPA annex.

5) Technical & organizational measures
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for storage; customer-managed keys supported in Dedicated/Private.
- Access controls: role-based access, least privilege, audited access logs (retained per contract).
- Separation: per-tenant isolation and optional prefix/KV cache isolation for sensitive workloads.
- Logging/retention: configurable retention windows; default retention for request logs is 30 days, can be shortened per contract.
- Certifications: SOC 2 Type II; penetration testing annually; we can provide SOC 2 report under NDA.

6) DPA annex specifics
- Deletion window: our standard is actioned within 30 days after termination or upon request unless constrained by law.
- Audit: customer audit rights are available with reasonable notice and under NDA.
- Liability/indemnity: our standard limits are in the attached annex; commercial can discuss exceptions.

7) Bespoke addenda
- We are open to reasonable redlines on the DPA annex. For material changes (e.g., extended audit windows, different liability caps) we will engage commercial.

Next steps:
- If you confirm the DPF cells you'd like prioritized, we'll populate your template and return it with redline suggestions for your DPA annex.
- If you need an executed DPA quickly, Marissa can coordinate internal approvals once Procurement confirms desired language.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
